description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:116-123

```rust
/// `parent_id` is `None` for the root level.  `case_insensitive`
/// controls the comparison (many file systems treat names
/// case-insensitively).
fn find_sibling_by_name(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    parent_id: Option<&jmap_types::Id>,
    name: &str,
    case_insensitive: bool,
) -> ...;
```

When `case_insensitive = true`, what algorithm does the backend use?

- ASCII fold only (a..z ↔ A..Z)?
- Unicode simple case fold (Default Case Folding)?
- Unicode full case fold (e.g. "ß" → "ss")?
- Turkish/Azerbaijani special-case folding ("I" ↔ "ı", "İ" ↔ "i")?
- HFS+ decomposition + fold (the macOS native behaviour)?
- ICU collation (locale-aware)?

The trait doc says nothing. The two test-double impls in this crate
disagree:
- `MemoryBackend::find_sibling_by_name` (memory.rs:662-704) uses
  `str::to_lowercase()` — Unicode simple lowercase, language-
  independent.
- `MockBackend::find_sibling_by_name` (lib.rs:440-457) also uses
  `str::to_lowercase()`, but the doc on `set_sibling` (lib.rs:230)
  says "Both case-sensitive and case-insensitive lookups use the
  lowercase key" — meaning case-sensitive lookups in the mock are
  actually case-insensitive. The contract is wrong in two layers.

Real-world impact: a JMAP client uploads a file "DOCUMENT.txt" to a
backend that stores filenames with Turkish-locale folding (where
"I" lowercases to "ı"). The reference Rust impl folds "DOCUMENT" to
"document"; the storage layer (e.g. an NTFS-backed CIFS share on a
Turkish-locale Windows server) folds it to "documenT" (with dotless
ı). The reference impl says no collision; the storage says
collision. The JMAP /set succeeds; the underlying filesystem rejects
the create. Client receives an unexpected backend error.

This is exactly the kind of footgun the API contract is supposed to
prevent. Either the trait must specify a canonical algorithm
(recommendation: Unicode Default Case Folding, NFC-normalized), or
the trait must take a callback so the caller controls folding.

Compare RFC 4791 (CalDAV) which explicitly defers to "the case
sensitivity of the resource path" — JMAP FileNode has no equivalent
hedge and the draft itself (draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13 §3.2.3
"compareCaseInsensitively") is also silent.

Suggested fix: add to the trait doc a normative MUST clause —
"Implementations MUST use Unicode Default Case Folding per Unicode
Standard Annex §3.13 over NFC-normalized input." If the workspace
position is that this is the implementer's call, document that
fact explicitly so a future migration between backends is not a
silent data-loss event.
title: FileNodeBackend::find_sibling_by_name case-folding algorithm is unspecified — interop hazard
